# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🖖 👌 ✌ 🤟 👌 🤟 🖐 👌 🖖 ☝ 👌 🖐 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝]

I see display `0`, a yellow light, and five wires in order: white, green, yellow, blue, red. I am sending these exact observations to Mute, who can consult the manual and tell Blind what to do. The gestures have no agreed code yet, so I will not rely on them.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb readings: display 0. Light is yellow. Wires numbered 1 through 5 are white, green, yellow, blue, red. Consult the manual and speak the exact safe action to Blind. Use plain words for all future instructions.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🖖 👌 ✌ 🤟 👌 🤟 🖐 👌 🖖 ☝ 👌 🖐 ✌ 👌 🖐 👌 🖐 🖖 🖐 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged. I still cannot hear the Mute’s spoken reply, and the gestures have no established code, so I cannot safely decode them. I will again direct the Mute to use the only reliable route to the Blind: plain spoken instructions.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot hear your speech or decode unagreed gestures. Please state the manual's exact safe action aloud to Blind in plain words, including any wire number, button, switch, or display operation.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐 👌 ☝ 🖖 👌 ✌ 🤟 👌 🤟 🖐 👌 🖖 ☝ 👌 🖐 ✌ 👌 🖐 👌 🖖 🖐 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

The visible bomb state remains unchanged. The previous gesture strings were sent before we had an agreed code, so I cannot safely interpret them. I am now establishing a compact code with Mute: the first gesture identifies the operation, and the second identifies a wire when applicable. I will then relay the decoded instruction to Blind in plain speech.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use this code now. Send exactly two gestures for the manual's safe action: first gesture 👍 means CUT a wire, 👎 means DO NOT CUT, 👌 means PRESS, ☝ means FLIP or TOGGLE, ✌ means TURN or SET. For a wire number, use ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖖=4, 🖐=5. If the action is not represented, send 🤝 alone and then we will establish another code. Do not use the old gesture strings.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb still shows display 0, yellow light, and wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Mute is now sending me a newly agreed gesture code for the manual's exact action; I will state it plainly.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌]

Mute’s new two-gesture message decodes under the agreed code as: cut wire 2. I am relaying that exact action to Blind, who can perform it.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The safe action is: cut wire 2, the green wire.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The previous action was correct, and the bomb has advanced to a new state. I now see display `0`, a blue light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 cut, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white. I am sending the complete state to Mute and asking for the next exact action using the established gesture code.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="New bomb state after the correct cut: display 0. Light is blue. Wires 1 yellow, 2 already CUT, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white. Consult the manual for the next safe action. If it is CUT wire N, send the agreed two gestures: 👍 then wire number. For other actions, use the agreed code or tell Blind plainly by speech.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🖐]

Mute’s message is 👍 followed by 🖐, which under our agreed code means cut wire 5. The bomb still shows display 0 and blue light; wire 5 is white. I am telling Blind to cut that wire.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The safe action is: cut wire 5, the white wire.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🖐]

The bomb has not changed, so wire 5 has not yet been cut. Mute has repeated the same code, 👍 🖐, confirming “cut wire 5.” I will repeat the plain instruction to Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed again: cut wire 5, the white wire. Do it now.")
```
